questions.q: What is the core difference between a Dimension and a Measure?
options: Dimensions are always blue and Measures are always green, with no exceptions
There is no real difference — the terms are interchangeable
Dimensions can only be dates; Measures can only be currency
Dimensions typically hold qualitative/categorical data; Measures typically hold numeric data that gets aggregated
questions.explain: Dimensions describe/categorize data (names, dates, geography); Measures are numeric fields that Tableau aggregates (usually with SUM) when placed in a view.

questions.q: Is discrete-vs-continuous the same split as Dimension-vs-Measure?
options: Yes, they are always identical — Dimensions are discrete and Measures are continuous with no exceptions
No — discrete/continuous is a separate distinction about how a field behaves in the view, independent of Dimension/Measure
No — discrete/continuous only applies to calculated fields
Yes, but only for date fields
questions.explain: A field can be converted between discrete and continuous independently of whether it's a Dimension or a Measure — dates are the clearest example of a field that can go either way.

questions.q: What does placing a continuous (green) field on the Columns or Rows shelf create?
options: A new calculated field automatically
A set of distinct text headers
A filter card
An axis — an unbroken numeric scale
questions.explain: Continuous fields form an unbroken range and create an axis, unlike discrete fields, which create separate headers.

questions.q: What does placing a discrete (blue) field on a shelf create?
options: A continuous numeric axis
Separate headers — one per distinct value in the field
A live database connection
A trend line automatically
questions.explain: Discrete fields have distinct separate values, so they produce individual headers/labels rather than a scale.

questions.q: How do you change whether a field behaves as discrete or continuous?
options: It's permanently fixed by the data source and cannot be changed
Only by editing the underlying database schema
Right-click the field and choose 'Convert to Discrete' or 'Convert to Continuous'
By changing the chart type in Show Me, which changes it automatically for every field
questions.explain: Right-clicking a field, in the Data pane or on a shelf, gives you 'Convert to Discrete' and 'Convert to Continuous' options.
